races.name: Dino Family Day At Fairyhouse Optional Claiming Race

runners_data.name: Henry Hudson
runners_data.note: A hold-up horse for David Marnane in fair form (7-5-4 recent), handles good ground well (2/3 on similar), but has been racing shorter and this 1m2f trip at Fairyhouse may test his stamina ceiling; Luke McAteer takes the ride with no weight claim.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last three but steadily progressing, improving to fourth last time from a fifth and a seventh before. Breaking from draw 9 after 28 days off, that upward trend makes him a leading danger.

runners_data.name: Mare Crisium
runners_data.note: K J Condon's filly carries an unresolved style tag and could drift into a prominent or even front-running role by default in a field devoid of natural pace-setters; has raced on softer ground (5th at 12f on soft, 8th at 12f on heavy) and faster conditions here may not flatter her.|
runners_data.comment: She found little when down the field earlier but rallied to fifth last time. Racing over today's trip again from draw 2, our rating shows modest ability with plenty still to prove.

runners_data.name: Pass The Buck
runners_data.note: Joseph Patrick O'Brien's stable in excellent form (T14: 9/56) and this hold-up type does stay — has placed over 10f on good ground — but the headgear flag (v: visor) and a tendency to find himself out of position in a field this hold-up heavy are genuine concerns; Sheridan takes over in the saddle.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five but rallying of late, up to fourth last time. Our rating makes him the one to beat from draw 4 despite a 28-day break, the reservation his patchy earlier form.

runners_data.name: Arizona Star
runners_data.note: Fades in the finish according to form notes, with six finishes in double digits over various trips, and the redistribution to midfield means Peter McCreery's charge is being asked to race closer than it naturally wants — style fit is discounted (0.90) and the form (0-0-3-0-6) offers minimal encouragement on faster ground.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and rarely featuring, with just a third three runs back standing out from a run of well-beaten efforts. She has covered today's trip before from draw 7, but there's little else to recommend her near the bottom of this field.

runners_data.name: Zitkala Sa
runners_data.note: Colin Keane is a major positive — his ability to get a horse into a perfect position mid-race is arguably the strongest tactical asset in this line-up — and the horse has shown a placed effort at 10f on good ground; naturally a hold-up type shuffled forward on the map, its chances hinge on Keane finding daylight in what promises to be a congested straight.|
runners_data.comment: A step forward when third last time out follows modest efforts before it, and our rating places her second in this field. First-time tongue-tie and cheekpieces add scope for more from draw 8, though a 37-day gap and no win in four starts are risks to weigh.

runners_data.name: Borora Aura
runners_data.note: Only six days since her last run (9th on good) and while Michael Mulvany has a recent winner over 14 days (1/12), the quick turnaround is a flag; the unresolved style tag makes her a possible pace-setter by default, and Gary Carroll may elect to exploit the leadership vacuum rather than surrender ground.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in six runs but far from disgraced, and a fourth last time out just six days ago suggests she's in form. She has covered today's trip and going before from draw 5, with first-time tongue-tie a fresh angle, though our rating keeps her only mid-field.

runners_data.name: Akissfromarose
runners_data.note: An OR of 120 stands out starkly against rivals rated in the 40s-69 range, yet the form line reads 0-0-9-0 and the fades-in-finish tag recurs throughout; racing here in headgear (tp) with a natural hold-up inclination and no evidence of handling fast ground, this horse looks a significant outlier whose rating tells a historical rather than current story.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts with barely a placed effort among them, and our rating leaves him bottom of this field by some way. Fourteen days since his last run, there is little in this profile to suggest he can trouble these rivals.

runners_data.name: Tenacious
runners_data.note: Mrs John Harrington's runner comes here after 51 days off — the longest absence in the field — with a best recent effort of 3rd at 8f on good, but the step back to 10f and the redistribution away from its natural rear position mean Nathan Crosse will need to settle it closer than ideal; the fade tag across multiple runs makes a winning finish hard to construct.|
runners_data.comment: A third three starts back is the highlight of an otherwise modest sequence, with her last two runs both unplaced, and our rating still places her third in this field. She has covered today's trip before from draw 3, though a 51-day absence and a winless run add real cause for concern.

runners_data.name: Music And Song
runners_data.note: Thomas Dowling's runner has run four times at 10f on good or good-to-soft and has not troubled the judge, with a best effort of 4th — 16 days between runs is fine physically, but the horse's natural hold-up style, fade tendency, and lowest OR in the field (40) combine to make this a very difficult winning scenario even if pace dynamics open up late.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in six starts, though a fourth last time out is an improvement on a spell that included two ninths. She has covered today's trip before from draw 1, with first-time cheekpieces a fresh twist, but our rating still leaves her in the lower half of this field.

races.paceDynamic: With no confirmed front-runner in this nine-runner field, the early pace is likely to be dawdling and tactical, with the field drifting together before accelerating late — a pattern that strongly favours horses who can travel smoothly through a compressed midfield and produce a sustained turn-of-foot in the straight. Mare Crisium and Borora Aura are the two runners with unresolved style tags (U) who may edge into a loose lead or prominent berth by default, simply because every other runner is nominally a hold-up type, creating a vacuum at the front. The bulk of the field — Henry Hudson, Pass The Buck, Arizona Star, Zitkala Sa, Tenacious, Music And Song, and Akissfromarose — all carry natural rear-end tendencies, meaning several are being mapped to midfield purely because the race cannot physically accommodate that many hold-up horses at the rear. With a slow crawl likely up front and a mass sprint home on Good to Firm ground, this race shape most benefits horses that can be ridden handily off the false pace, travel without cover, and quicken efficiently in the final two furlongs — a profile that suits whatever horse can command a prominent position by default rather than by design.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Slow Pace Sprint Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the field crawls early and the race degenerates into a flat-out sprint over the final two furlongs on fast ground.
scenarios.body: The absence of genuine front-runners means the tempo will be set reluctantly, compressing the field and turning the race into a dash from two out; horses ridden prominently by default — particularly Mare Crisium and Borora Aura — get a decisive positional advantage over the true hold-up types caught cold.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Lands Blow
scenarios.trigger: If a genuine hold-up runner manages to secure an ideal position just off the pace and produces a clean late run in the straight.
scenarios.body: With most of the field bunched and jostling for position, a horse that naturally settles in mid-division and picks off rivals in the closing stages could exploit the congestion; Zitkala Sa with Colin Keane in the saddle and Tenacious, trained by Mrs John Harrington, are the most credible beneficiaries if a clean passage materialises.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Mare Crisium or Borora Aura establishes a clear lead early and dictates a strong, uncontested gallop that stretches the field.
scenarios.body: A genuine pace on Good to Firm ground over 1m2f would place a premium on stamina and front-running efficiency, isolating the field's slow-starting hold-up horses who lack the tactical speed to bridge a meaningful gap; the horse able to control the tempo from the front would have a significant advantage in what is a low-quality optional claimer.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Wide-Open Bunched Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is so slow that the entire field arrives at the final furlong in a heap and the result is decided by raw speed and luck in running.
scenarios.body: In a chaotic finish across the full width of the track, any runner with a clear lane could snatch the prize regardless of running style, handing the race to whoever avoids traffic — Pass The Buck and Henry Hudson both have the physical scope to benefit from a fortunate break in a pell-mell finish.

watchPoints.text: Borora Aura's quick six-day turnaround combined with Gary Carroll potentially exploiting the pace vacuum — if she jumps cleanly and takes the initiative, the hold-up field will be chasing from the front and she could prove very hard to reel in.

Colin Keane on Zitkala Sa is the standout jockey-horse combination for navigating a compressed, slow-run race — watch for him to position three or four lengths off the false pace and deliver a challenge in the widest lane at the two-furlong marker.

The field is overloaded with hold-up types, meaning traffic and interference in the straight are near-certain; any horse drawn to the outside and asked to make a wide run late could be caught in a chain of switching horses — watch for crowding between the two-furlong pole and the final furlong.

Akissfromarose's OR of 120 versus rivals in the 40-69 band invites scrutiny — if this rating is current and accurate it is a different race entirely, but the 0-0-9-0 form and repeated fade notes suggest the rating is stale; do not over-weight it without understanding the origin.

Good to Firm conditions are confirmed for this race — faster than the soft and heavy surfaces several runners (Mare Crisium, Pass The Buck, Arizona Star) have recently contested, and the going shift could expose any stamina or action concerns on the faster surface at the 1m2f trip.

races.name: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Fillies Maiden
Irish Stallion Farms EBF (C & G) Maiden
Fairyhouse Winter Festival 28th & 29th November Rated Race

runners_data.name: Royal Hollow
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner in the race; Sam Coen's 5lb claim is useful, trainer Slattery sends this 8-year-old out on a 16-day turnaround with solid recent form including a course win over course and distance on Soft, and the style fit rating suggests they will get first run but the drop back to a prominent label slightly flatters their staying chance if challenged.
runners_data.comment: Runner-up last time out and with a win earlier in this sequence, she brings the strongest recent form into this, and our rating makes her the one to beat. Proven over today's trip, a below-par run three starts back is the only blip on an otherwise progressive profile.

runners_data.name: Light Up The Dark
runners_data.note: Joseph O'Brien's 5-year-old returns from a 91-day break having won last time at 13f on Good and is strongly placed with Colin Keane's stable's 11-from-70 form in 14 days; trips of 13-18f in recent history suit today's 1m6f and this horse can travel prominently without burning resources.
runners_data.comment: Won last time out to cap a race-fit spell that also included a third and an earlier win, giving her strong claims on figures behind only the selection. Proven over today's trip, a 91-day absence since is the obvious concern to work around.

runners_data.name: Buddy One
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up type returning from a 298-day absence — the longest layoff in this field — which is a significant flag for a 9-year-old; the form string shows blanks on the flat at shorter trips and the 119-day jumps break compounds the fitness question, needing a strongly-run race he may simply not be fit enough to exploit.
runners_data.comment: A win two starts back shows he has ability, but he was unplaced last time. He has covered today's trip before, and our rating still keeps him firmly among the leading contenders on a workable racing weight of 134 lb.

runners_data.name: Tounsivator
runners_data.note: Willie Mullins sends out this 5-year-old on a 269-day absence with Colin Keane aboard, and the horse's natural prominence suits sitting just off the pace; three wins and four places on similar going in the historical record suggest ability on the surface, but the long layoff on a tight 14-day trainer stat of 15/111 makes confidence hard.
runners_data.comment: A win three starts back points to genuine ability, but he finished down the field last time out and has not run for 269 days since. He carries 134 lb, and our rating still rates him a threat, though the long absence is the major risk.

runners_data.name: Sir Callisto
runners_data.note: A natural front-running type whose last three wins came at 12f on Standard, which is shorter than today's 1m6f trip; headgear worn, and the redistribution note confirms this horse cannot comfortably find its preferred prominent position in a field this stacked with forward-travelling types, which costs it a significant tactical advantage.
runners_data.comment: A win three starts back and consistent frame efforts either side highlight genuine ability, though he found nothing when unplaced last time out. Fresh off a 37-day break and our rating still puts him in the middle of this field, leaving a case both for and against him.

runners_data.name: Chutzpal
runners_data.note: Henry De Bromhead's 7-year-old is a genuine prominent racer who has been mapped back to midfield because the race already has more forward types than can be accommodated; the headgear (blinkers) and a 45-day break suggest they could push up regardless, but the four wins from 15 runs on Good-equivalent going shows solid surface compatibility.
runners_data.comment: A win three starts back and three more placed efforts in this spell paint a picture of solid, consistent ability, but he was unplaced last time out. He has covered today's trip before, and first-time blinkers add intrigue, though our rating leaves him down among the outsiders here.

runners_data.name: Not Just Any Eagle
runners_data.note: A 7lb-claiming apprentice, Robyn Donaghue-Leahy, rides this hold-up 7-year-old whose recent form figures of 79-070 show a horse badly out of form; the sim-going record of 1 win from 15 at similar ground conditions is uninspiring and a truly run gallop would be needed for this profile to land in the placings.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts without ever really threatening, finishing no better than seventh across that run. He has covered today's trip and going before, and our rating - a shade higher than his official mark - hints at more solid ability than the bare results suggest.

runners_data.name: Pavilion End
runners_data.note: Charles O'Brien's 6-year-old has a sequence of double-figure finishes in recent starts and zero wins from 15 runs on comparable going; the horse's true running style is hold-up but has been mapped to midfield — the form profile alone makes it hard to make a case regardless of tactical positioning, and the 0 wins from 4 runners for the trainer in the last 14 days adds no optimism.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and fading badly through that run, from a third down to consecutive unplaced efforts most recently. He has covered today's trip before, but our rating leaves him at the bottom of this field, and there is little here to inspire confidence.

races.paceDynamic: Royal Hollow is the clear and sole confirmed front-runner here, and with no genuine challenger for the lead, they are set to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop over this 1m6f trip on Good to Firm ground at Fairyhouse. Light Up The Dark and Tounsivator will press forward from their prominent positions and ensure Royal Hollow is not entirely unchallenged, but neither is a true pace-forcing type, so the tempo should remain honest rather than scorching. This race shape firmly favours hold-up or prominent horses with the ability to travel smoothly through the race and produce a sustained finish — particularly those who can sit within striking distance without burning fuel early. The field actually contains more prominent-style types than the pace map can accommodate: Sir Callisto, Chutzpal, and Pavilion End are all natural forwardly-placed or hold-up horses who cannot all secure their preferred positions, and of those, Sir Callisto and Chutzpal are most likely to press forward if they assert early, while Pavilion End is most likely to be shuffled back.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Royal Hollow Dictates Wire-to-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Royal Hollow is allowed to bowl along unchallenged at a comfortable gallop and the prominent posse behind never applies sufficient pressure to unsettle their rhythm.
scenarios.body: Royal Hollow, settled into an uncontested lead, conserves enough energy to resist challengers in the straight on the Good to Firm surface, with the moderate pace suiting a horse who can relax and quicken from the front at this trip.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Horse Sweeps Past Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace set by Royal Hollow is just honest enough to drain their finishing reserves and a prominent-placed rival delivers a well-timed challenge in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Light Up The Dark, fresh off a 91-day break and trained by Joseph O'Brien with a strong 14-day strike rate, is ideally positioned to travel prominently and hit the line strongest if the leader has left just enough on the clock.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Runs On Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves genuinely strong enough to stretch the field and create a truly run race that rewards horses who have been conserving energy from the rear.
scenarios.body: Buddy One or Not Just Any Eagle, both true hold-up types, would need the race to develop at a genuinely searching tempo to get competitive late, and Buddy One's lengthy absence (298 days) adds significant risk to any reliance on this shape.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Tactical Mess
scenarios.trigger: If multiple prominent types jostle for position early — particularly if Sir Callisto or Chutzpal push forward out of their redistributed slots — creating an uneven or bunched gallop that produces an unpredictable finish.
scenarios.body: A chaotic early race with several horses out of their natural position could produce a false pace that scrambles the form book, but this field lacks the confirmed pace war ingredients to make this shape likely.

watchPoints.text: Royal Hollow — if they pinged the gates and build an early three-length cushion, the race is effectively over by halfway as no confirmed pace rival exists to apply sustained pressure.

Sir Callisto and Chutzpal — both natural prominent types who have been redistributed; if either decides to push forward aggressively early, the pace could quicken unexpectedly and unsettle Royal Hollow's rhythm, changing the entire shape of the race.

Light Up The Dark — a 91-day break for a Joseph O'Brien yard running at 11/70 in the last fortnight; if they show any bounce or ring-rustiness early, their chance evaporates, but if they travel sweetly they are the principal danger to the leader.

Tounsivator — 269 days off the track is an enormous query at any age but particularly for a 5-year-old; monitor in the paddock for condition and behaviour, as a visually well-prepared horse from Mullins at any price would upgrade their claims markedly.

Buddy One — 298 days absent and a 9-year-old; regardless of ability, if this horse is not visually sharp in the pre-parade ring the fitness concern is real enough to remove them from any serious consideration in race-shape matching.

races.name: Darley Irish EBF Stanerra Stakes (Fillies' & Mares' Group 3)

runners_data.name: Floresta
runners_data.note: Proven at the trip with two wins at 14f and best form on Good ground; P Ryan's daughter of Deep Impact has the profile to track the pace comfortably from her natural prominent slot and convert here if she recaptures her Listed-winning form.
runners_data.comment: Two wins in her last five starts show latent ability, though she was unplaced last time out and hasn't run for 64 days. She has covered today's trip before and our rating puts her mid-division on 95.

runners_data.name: Galileo Dame
runners_data.note: Best form has come over 14-16f on Heavier ground, winning twice at Leopardstown on Heavy; her natural desire to race prominently is compromised in this field because there simply isn't room, so she must operate further back than ideal and her good-to-firm record (0W in 15 tries on similar ground) raises a genuine concern.
runners_data.comment: Without a win in her last five starts, she found the frame when second three runs back, and our rating makes a strong case for more to come fresh off a 22-day break. Proven over today's trip and ground, she is our pick to go well.

runners_data.name: Goodie Two Shoes
runners_data.note: The only confirmed pace-setter in the race; two wins at 14-16f on Good ground and top-rated in the field at OR 108, she carries 135lbs but controls her own destiny from the front and her 19-day turnaround is straightforward.
runners_data.comment: Two wins in her last five starts show solid ability, and our rating makes her the one to beat just 19 days after her latest outing. First-time tongue-tie adds interest, but a below-par eighth last time out is the risk to weigh.

runners_data.name: Jannah Star
runners_data.note: No win in 8 career starts and a form string of 34-468 points to a horse who struggles to convert; her preference for racing up with the pace is a problem here given the traffic, and finishing eighth last time over 12f on Good is not an encouraging trail into a Group 3.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and fading through that run - 4th, 4th, 6th, then 8th last time out - which is hard to ignore. She has raced over today's trip before and a 24-day break may freshen her, though little here inspires confidence.

runners_data.name: Nuit
runners_data.note: Colin Keane takes over on a mare who finished second at Listowey Flat and has placed on Good ground before; she wants to be prominent but the redistribution issue means she may not get that luxury, and 64 days off means fitness must be assumed, not proven.
runners_data.comment: Without a win in her last five starts, she has stayed competitive with a second two starts back and a couple of minor placings in that spell. A 64-day absence and first-time tongue-tie add uncertainty, but our rating keeps her in the mix.

runners_data.name: Perfect Your Craft
runners_data.note: Won over 12f on Good and placed at 10f, so the step up to 1m6f is a live stamina question; William Lee rides and the horse wears a hood, which suggests a tendency to switch off — if the hood works and she travels sweetly from her natural prominent position, the trip may be within range.
runners_data.comment: A near-miss second two starts back and a win four back point to solid ability, and our rating puts her firmly among the leading players. First-time cheekpieces could sharpen her further, though a below-par fifth last time out is the risk to note.

runners_data.name: Bloom
runners_data.note: Aidan O'Brien's three-year-old carries a 13lb age allowance and won over 8f on Good; all five career runs are on Good ground (strong going suitability), but this 1m6f trip is a significant jump from her last run over 12f and stamina is unproven at the top level.
runners_data.comment: A win four starts back and consecutive thirds around it point to real claims, and she has run over today's going before. Our rating keeps her among the leading dangers at a workable 122 lb, though a below-par seventh last time out is the risk to note.

runners_data.name: Dreamkeeper
runners_data.note: Won over 12f on Good just eight days ago, so the turnaround is sharp for a three-year-old; Noel Meade's filly naturally wants to be prominent but is mapped to midfield given the field's shape, meaning Gavin Ryan will need to manage her keenness in unfamiliar territory.
runners_data.comment: A win two starts back is the highlight of modest recent form either side of it, and our rating places her firmly at the foot of this field. She is fresh from just an 8-day break, but there's little in these figures to make a strong case.

runners_data.name: Ice Dancer
runners_data.note: The field's only genuine hold-up horse, but a poor record at 12f on Good (4/6 placed) and still maiden-like in Group company; Ronan Whelan will look to deliver her late, and if the pace collapses she is the horse most naturally suited to sweeping from the rear.
runners_data.comment: A win five starts back is a distant memory, with recent form sliding to a ninth last time after back-to-back sevenths. First-time blinkers offer a sliver of hope, but the trend is hard to ignore.

races.paceDynamic: Goodie Two Shoes is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine pressure expected to materialize from behind, she will control this race from the front at a sustainable gallop on Good to Firm ground over 1m6f. Floresta, Bloom, and Perfect Your Craft will try to sit prominent behind her, but the redistribution problem is significant: Nuit, Galileo Dame, Jannah Star, and Dreamkeeper are all natural prominent types who cannot all secure their preferred position in a field of nine, meaning several will be forced to race in unfamiliar midfield territory. The race shape should therefore resolve into a single-file, controlled affair with Goodie Two Shoes dictating tempo and a short, sharp finish — most likely decided by those who can travel close to the pace without burning energy fighting for position. This shape strongly favours genuine prominent racers who can sit second or third in a slowly-run-turned-quick, positional contest, and works against redistributed types who will spend energy racing out of role.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Goodie Two Shoes Dictates Unopposed
scenarios.trigger: If Goodie Two Shoes leads uncontested at a controlled tempo and quickens entering the straight, rewarding those who tracked her closely.
scenarios.body: She sets a sustainable fractions on good-to-firm ground and turns the race into a test of late acceleration from close range, where prominent racers who saved energy in slots two and three hold the decisive edge.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Challenge Entering Straight
scenarios.trigger: If Floresta or Bloom travels powerfully enough to join Goodie Two Shoes turning in, forcing a two-way battle that stretches the field.
scenarios.body: The pace lifts noticeably earlier than the solo-lead scenario, compressing the finish and rewarding a horse with both stamina and tactical speed; those who saved ground in fourth or fifth can also benefit if the leading pair empty.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Late Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Goodie Two Shoes overextends from the front on good-to-firm and weakens inside the final furlong, gifting the race to those tracking at a distance.
scenarios.body: The tempo paradoxically proves too hot for the leader despite the solo nature, opening a gap for horses who sat just off the pace rather than genuine hold-up types; Ice Dancer's hold-up style and Bloom's turn of foot make them relevant.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos From Redistribution Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If multiple prominent types fight for early positions behind Goodie Two Shoes, burning energy and producing a truly messy, uneven tempo.
scenarios.body: Horses dragged into faster fractions through the middle stages fail to sustain it home, and a horse who managed to slot quietly into midfield and travel economically benefits from the disorder in the leading group.

watchPoints.text: Goodie Two Shoes holds all the pace cards — if she jumps cleanly and is allowed a clear lead, watch whether any rider attempts to go with her early, as any challenge could either string the race out dangerously or simply burn out a rival who cannot sustain it.

Nuit, Galileo Dame, Jannah Star, and Dreamkeeper are all trying to race in the same two or three positions behind the leader — watch the first two furlongs for crowding and bumping as these redistributed prominent types jostle for the same slots.

Bloom's stamina at 1m6f is untested — she has never raced beyond 12f, and if the pace is compressed by Goodie Two Shoes quickening turning in, watch whether she simply finds the trip beyond her before the finish.

Perfect Your Craft wears a hood (first-time or repeat); in a race where settling is critical over this marathon trip, watch how she travels through the first half of the race to gauge whether the hood is working as intended.

Ice Dancer has shown no form on turf beyond placing at 12f on Good (0W0P at 12f on Good); as a hold-up horse in a race likely to produce a compact finish, watch whether Ronan Whelan can find any daylight through a field that may be bunched late.

races.name: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Maiden

runners_data.name: Banshof
runners_data.note: 4yo with a form string of 6-8 over shorter trips, lightly raced and an unknown quantity at 7f; Scott McCullagh/Matthew Smith combination has place form from recent runs but no win, and the step up in trip is an uncertainty rather than a clear positive.

runners_data.name: Pettus Bridge
runners_data.note: Denise Foster-trained 4yo whose only run produced an 11th of 12 over 1m2f on Good ground; the drop to 7f helps the stamina question but the fades-in-finish flag and unraced profile at this distance makes this a speculative entry.

runners_data.name: Auguste Gusteau
runners_data.note: Trainer Cahill has limited recent strike rate; this horse is a natural hold-up type by profile, but with the rear of the field congested it is likely to find itself racing further forward than ideal — form over 5-6f suggests ability but the redistribution away from a true back-of-field role tempers the chance here.

runners_data.name: Bamako Beach
runners_data.note: The race's sole confirmed front-runner, placed twice at this course and distance on Good and Soft ground, handled by Colin Keane; the lone-leader role suits but the STYLE_FIT note on the map is a reminder that any pace injection from rivals would disturb his rhythm.

runners_data.name: Chloe's Boy
runners_data.note: H Rogers 3yo whose only run ended in 14th over 1m on Good; a genuine hold-up horse by nature but the crowded rear means it will likely be shuffled into mid-division — the fades-in-finish flag compounds the difficulty of making an impact from that compromised berth.

runners_data.name: Cladach
runners_data.note: Joseph Patrick O'Brien debut runner for whom no form is available; the trainer's powerful 14-day record (10/67) is the key pointer, and first-time-out O'Brien juveniles at this track deserve respect, though going is UNKNOWN and style is unclassified.

runners_data.name: Coolshine
runners_data.note: K A Heffernan-trained 3yo who has finished 9th and 11th over 7-8f on Good and Soft; the fades-in-finish flag is a consistent pattern and the hold-up style makes progress against a sustainable pace difficult — hard to see the angle here.

runners_data.name: Farewell To Arms
runners_data.note: Charles O'Brien's 3yo returns after 54 days off following runs of 8th and 13th over 8f; the hold-up style, fades-in-finish flag, and step down in trip from maiden mile runs suggests this horse needs more pace than Bamako Beach is likely to generate.

runners_data.name: Passage Of Power
runners_data.note: Joseph Patrick O'Brien 3yo whose sole run was a promising 3rd of 6 over 6f at the Curragh — the step up to 7f is logical, but 176 days off is a significant fitness query; if ready, the class angle and unexposed profile make this an interesting unknown.

runners_data.name: Shay's Dream
runners_data.note: O'Brien-trained hold-up horse whose last two runs have yielded a 10th and 14th; the fades-in-finish flag and poor form cycle make it difficult to build a case, and a 28-day break has not produced any obvious improvement indicator.

runners_data.name: Sindagan
runners_data.note: JP Murtagh's 3yo is the most exposed horse in the race with placed form at 7f on Soft and Heavy — the step to Good To Firm is a going query but the recent run of 3-2-4-3 shows consistent proximity; Ben Coen rides and a prominent style suits this race shape well.

runners_data.name: Storzando
runners_data.note: Michael Mulvany debut runner with no form on record; the going is listed as UNKNOWN and the style unclassified — without trainer firepower to match O'Brien, this is the more speculative of the two unexposed runners.

runners_data.name: Thumama Sands
runners_data.note: Adrian McGuinness 3yo who has finished 11th and 14th over 7f; the fades-in-finish flag is confirmed across both runs, the going has consistently been a challenge, and there is no form pointer to suggest improvement on Good To Firm today.

runners_data.name: Goomah
runners_data.note: Natalia Lupini's hold-up specialist with a placed run over 7f on Good in its form string — genuinely suited by this trip, but with the back of the field over-populated it will be forced to race in mid-division rather than its preferred position; the STYLE_FIT discount is real, though it retains some each-way profile if the pace becomes searching.

runners_data.name: Little Sure Shot
runners_data.note: Henry De Bromhead's 3yo returns after 102 days wearing a hood; placed at 2nd over 8f on Good and 2nd over 6f on Heavy, so the 7f trip is a fair median, but the lengthy break and true hold-up nature — redistributed into mid-division due to field congestion — mean it will need things to fall its way.

races.paceDynamic: Bamako Beach is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 15-runner maiden and, with no genuine pace rival to push him, Colin Keane is expected to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front over the 7f Fairyhouse straight. The Good To Firm conditions will keep the pace honest rather than truly searching, meaning the early fractions are unlikely to be punishing enough to fully set up a late rush from the back of the field. Sindagan and Passage Of Power are the most credible prominent stalkers who can sit just off Bamako Beach and strike in the straight, while the bulk of the field — Auguste Gusteau, Chloe's Boy, Goomah, and Little Sure Shot — are genuine hold-up types redistributed into midfield on the map because the rear of the field is over-subscribed; they are unlikely to secure their natural position and will be racing out of role to varying degrees. The race shape strongly favours horses who can settle just off the pace and sustain their run through the final two furlongs — prominent-to-midfield stalkers who do not need a truly strong gallop to deliver their finishing effort.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Bamako Beach Controls Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Bamako Beach is allowed to stride comfortably into a lead that is never seriously threatened, setting a steady-to-moderate tempo on the Good To Firm ground.
scenarios.body: Keane dictates the fractions from a wide draw, the field settles into a procession, and the horses closest to him in the first half of the race are best placed as the pace lifts inside the final two furlongs. Prominent and close-stalking types who get an uncontested first two furlongs to travel within themselves are the prime beneficiaries in this shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Stalkers Overhaul Pace
scenarios.trigger: If the Good To Firm ground produces a faster-than-expected early tempo and Bamako Beach ties up late, allowing the best-travelled prominent horses to stride past.
scenarios.body: Horses who have settled just off the pace conserve energy through the middle of the race and find an extra gear in the final furlong that the leader cannot match. Sindagan's course-and-distance placed form and Passage Of Power's class angle make them the most likely to capitalise in this shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Types Finish Through
scenarios.trigger: If the tempo is genuinely brisk and the pace combusts in the final furlong, leaving a gap for horses who have been held up in mid-division to pick up the pieces.
scenarios.body: Auguste Gusteau and Goomah, though racing out of their natural hold-up role, are the most capable of sustaining a late run if the race develops into a truly run affair that stretches the field. The STYLE_FIT discount applies — both are unlikely to be exactly where they want to be — but a truly run race narrows that disadvantage.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Debutants Surprise Field
scenarios.trigger: If one of the lightly-raced or debut runners — Cladach or Storzando — shows previously unseen ability and proves well above the form of the exposed runners.
scenarios.body: Joseph Patrick O'Brien's Cladach is completely unexposed and trainer clout (10/67 in 14 days) signals a live chance on debut if the horse has been readied for this moment. Storzando is similarly unknown but lacks the stable firepower behind it, making Cladach the stronger candidate in this low-probability shape.

watchPoints.text: Cladach and Storzando are both debut runners with zero exposed form — watch the market moves on both, particularly Cladach given Joseph Patrick O'Brien's 10/67 14-day strike rate, as any significant market move would upgrade this runner from a speculative chance to a serious contender.

Bamako Beach is the lone confirmed pace-setter but carries a STYLE_FIT flag of 0.92 — if any of the nominally prominent horses such as Sindagan or Passage Of Power push forward aggressively at the start, Bamako Beach could find itself in a contested lead that undermines its chance of controlling the race.

Sindagan arrives on Good To Firm having run exclusively on Soft, Heavy and Yielding ground — watch for any visible signs of the faster surface affecting its action in the early stages, as a going concern here would significantly alter the race's most credible stalking contender.

Little Sure Shot returns after 102 days off and is fitted with a hood — watch its behaviour in the preliminaries and how it jumps from the stalls, as a hold-up horse needs a clean start to have any hope of making ground from a compromised mid-division position.

The cluster of hold-up types — Auguste Gusteau, Chloe's Boy, Goomah, and Little Sure Shot — will all be jostling for similar space in the first two furlongs; watch for crowding and interference in the early stages that could cost any one of them a clean passage.

races.name: Winter Festival Early Bird Tickets From 20 Euros Handicap

runners_data.name: Rahmi
runners_data.note: Top-rated runner at OR 102 with Ben Coen booked, holds clear Good-ground form at 7f (won 1/7f/GOO) and the trip is not a concern, but races from hold-up and the likely steady tempo under Indigo Dream's control works against generating a meaningful late run from the rear.
runners_data.comment: Proven over today's trip and fresh from a 24-day break, Rahmi is the pick of this seven on our figures (104) with the fastest speed rating too; his placings have cooled since winning five starts back, but the level here makes him hard to beat.

runners_data.name: Tolebi
runners_data.note: Gary Carroll partner has very modest recent form figures (9th, 4th, 12th) and his two best going runs at 7f on Good produced 9th and 4th; stepping back from shorter trips and struggling for consistency, no strong positional or tactical angle in this shape.
runners_data.comment: Yet to win in his last five, Tolebi ran a below-par ninth last time but had shown much more with a fourth before that, and a quick 12-day turnaround suggests untapped fitness. Second on our figures and proven over this trip, he's the main threat if bouncing back.

runners_data.name: Bishopton
runners_data.note: Active yard (T14: 2/8) and Chris Hayes in the saddle lends confidence; ran 2nd and 1st at this general trip-and-going profile, and his prominent style suits a race where sitting just behind the leader is the ideal tactical slot at Fairyhouse over 7f.
runners_data.comment: Bishopton won four starts back but has since faded to a below-par sixth last time. Already proven over today's trip and this going, and fourth on our figures with a solid speed rating (80), he's fit to bounce back on a quick 11-day turnaround.

runners_data.name: Exquisite Acclaim
runners_data.note: A confirmed hold-up performer whose true style has been absorbed into the midfield mapping because the rear is overpopulated — visor on, trainer McGuinness in decent form (T14: 2/30), but the horse's best recent runs came on Standout ground over 8f and the shift to 7f Good To Firm with a style mismatch is a meaningful double concern.
runners_data.comment: Exquisite Acclaim won five starts back and has been inconsistent since, including a below-par seventh last time, but first-time visor could sharpen him up. Third on our figures and proven over today's trip and this ground, he's a threat if the headgear switch pays off.

runners_data.name: Indigo Dream
runners_data.note: The only confirmed front-runner in the field and therefore almost certain to secure a clear lead from the outset; tongue-tie applied, but the STYLE_FIT tag reflects that in a more truly run race she could be vulnerable — on this pace map, her ability to set her own fractions is the single biggest tactical advantage in the race.
runners_data.comment: Yet to win in six runs and below-par (8th) two starts back, Indigo Dream did show ability with two earlier runner-up efforts. Proven over today's trip and quick back within 12 days, but ranked only sixth of seven on our figures, she has plenty to find.

runners_data.name: Glory To Be
runners_data.note: Wayne Lordan partner ran 2nd over 6f Good recently and has five placings in his last six at this level; prominent style is perfectly suited to sitting just off Indigo Dream's pace and mounting a sustained challenge, though 8f last time out may have left a mark and 7d since last run is on the fresh side.
runners_data.comment: A runner-up effort last time, quick back within 7 days, suggests Glory To Be is in form, and she won five starts back too. First-time cheekpieces and a strong speed figure (85) add appeal, but an official mark of just 79 says there's more to prove.

runners_data.name: I Bid You Ajou
runners_data.note: Gavin Ryan takes over on a horse with a genuinely prominent racing style who has been redistributed to midfield because too many runners want the same real estate early; three wins from 6f Good to Firm runs suggest the horse has the raw ability, but racing outside his natural slot on a moderate tempo is a concrete disadvantage, and the 31-day absence adds a small fitness query.
runners_data.comment: Yet to win in six starts despite a pair of runner-up efforts, I Bid You Ajou ranks bottom of seven on our figures and is back from a 31-day absence. Proven over today's trip and going, a place looks more realistic than a win.

races.paceDynamic: Indigo Dream is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with only two other genuine prominent types (Bishopton and Glory To Be) to contest early position, she should be able to dictate at a sustainable gallop on Good To Firm ground over this flat Fairyhouse 7f. That uncontested lead will set a steady-to-moderate tempo, compressing the field and making it difficult for true hold-up horses to generate the momentum they need from the rear. The field holds more prominent-leaning runners than the pace map can naturally accommodate — Indigo Dream is best-placed to secure the front, while I Bid You Ajou is the most likely to find herself unable to get her preferred slot and forced to settle deeper than ideal. This race shape strongly favours prominent racers who can travel close to the pace and pick off a tiring leader in the final furlong, rather than hold-up horses attempting to generate a sustained late run off an insufficient gallop.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Indigo Dream Controls Lead
scenarios.trigger: If Indigo Dream pinges the gate and settles into an uncontested lead, dictating a fair but manageable fractions on the Good To Firm surface.
scenarios.body: Indigo Dream rolls along unchallenged through the early and middle stages, and the steady tempo means closers never generate enough momentum to reel her in late; the race becomes a test of stamina and tactical positioning rather than raw speed.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Poacher Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Bishopton or Glory To Be tracks Indigo Dream closely and produces a decisive challenge in the final 2f, overwhelming a pace-set leader who has given too much early.
scenarios.body: The steady gallop suits a patient prominent runner who has conserved energy in second or third, and one of these two has the class and course form to pounce decisively once Indigo Dream is headed; Bishopton's recent 7f Fairyhouse form and OR makes her the more interesting of the pair.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closer Gets Home
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves quicker than expected and the leaders tire badly inside the final furlong, creating a rare opportunity for a hold-up horse to swoop.
scenarios.body: Rahmi is the most credible hold-up type in the field, with genuine Good ground form at this trip and a top jockey in Ben Coen who can time a run; however, the likely moderate tempo means ground to make up late is the least favoured outcome, and her recent form figures are inconsistent.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If Indigo Dream sets a falsely slow pace that implodes in the final 2f, causing the whole field to bunch and produce an unpredictable sprint finish.
scenarios.body: In this unlikely scenario mid-division horses like I Bid You Ajou and Exquisite Acclaim — who are mapped out of their natural roles — could benefit from a messy race where tactical positioning becomes irrelevant and raw sprint ability decides matters; both carry style-fit discounts and this shape requires things to go very wrong for the principals.

watchPoints.text: Watch Indigo Dream's gate break — if she misses the start or is slow to stride, the entire pace map collapses and Bishopton or Glory To Be could immediately inherit the lead on their own terms.

Glory To Be returns just 7 days after her last run; if she shows any sign of freshness or early exuberance she could push Indigo Dream into a faster-than-expected gallop, which would flip the race in favour of hold-up types like Rahmi.

I Bid You Ajou will almost certainly be shuffled back from her natural prominent position in the early stages — watch whether Gavin Ryan accepts the midfield slot quietly or attempts to push forward, as the latter could cause a flurry of early movement and disrupt the shape entirely.

Ben Coen on Rahmi will need to find a racing line quickly on a potentially compressed 7f flat track if the tempo is truly moderate — if the field strings out early he has a chance, but if they bunch she will have traffic to navigate in the straight.

races.name: Racing Again September 21st Handicap

runners_data.name: Faoladh
runners_data.note: The sole genuine pace-setter and master of this race shape — Adam Browne-Souza gets a lone lead on Good to Firm ground at the right trip, with 10/15 similar-going efforts providing the bedrock, though the OR=72 ceiling and a modest recent run string (4th, 6th last two) remind that domination is not the same as winning.
runners_data.comment: Faoladh won two starts back. Only sixth last time, but first-time tongue-tie may sharpen him. Fourth on our figures with a useful speed rating (78) and proven over today's trip and going, he's competitive without looking the standout.

runners_data.name: Chester Nimitz
runners_data.note: Nicola Burns (5lb claim) partners a four-year-old whose sole win came over 6f on Good, and while 8/12 similar-going runs suggest he handles this surface, back-to-back 9ths over 8f before a 10th on handicap debut are hard to ignore — the step back to 7f for a prominent runner is the one angle to take seriously.
runners_data.comment: Chester Nimitz tops our figures at 79 having won four starts back, but back-to-back below-par ninths since are hard to ignore. Already proven over today's trip and quick to return within 12 days, he's the one to beat on rating if repeating that decisive form.

runners_data.name: Loingseoir
runners_data.note: A decade-old veteran whose best form was over this 7f trip, but four of his last five runs came on Soft or Heavy and his lone Good-ground run in the relevant distance returned a 7th — M C Grassick's charge needs more cut underfoot to be at his best and that concern is live tonight.
runners_data.comment: Yet to win in five starts but fairly consistent with a pair of fourths last twice, Loingseoir could find more with first-time tongue-tie applied. Third on our figures despite a modest mark of 70 and proven over today's trip, a 27-day gap is the main query.

runners_data.name: Shoot To Kill
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse (headgear: p) who found 2nd over 7f on Good last time — his two wins and four places all came on a variety of surfaces confirming versatility, but the 27-day absence and an OR of 70 in a competitive handicap means he needs a strongly-run race to get home from off the pace.
runners_data.comment: A below-par run last time follows solid placed efforts two and three starts back, and first-time cheekpieces should sharpen his finish nicely. Yet to win in his last five starts, but the placed form claims make him one to take seriously over this ground and trip.

runners_data.name: Surpass And Shine
runners_data.note: Robyn Donaghue-Leahy (7lb) partners a three-year-old with two wins at 5f on Good, but today's 7f trip is uncharted territory and 334 days off the track is a substantial fitness concern — Patrick J Flynn has a quiet recent record and there are too many unknowns to trust this profile at a handicap mark of OR=69.
runners_data.comment: Surpass And Shine won twice in his last five starts, but both wins came before a pair of below-par efforts, and he now returns from a lengthy 334-day absence. Proven over today's trip and going, the ability is there but the long layoff is a real concern.

runners_data.name: Imperial Dream
runners_data.note: Dropped back from 8f to 7f where his best recent run was a 2nd on Soft/Standard at that distance — Alan Persse (5lb) has a route in from 65 days off the track, and as a natural hold-up horse the tactical squeeze in this big field makes it hard for him to produce his best without a properly strong gallop.
runners_data.comment: Second on our figures despite below-par efforts in his last two starts, Imperial Dream ran creditably before that with a fourth and a second. Proven over today's trip and going and returning after a 65-day gap, the main question is whether that recent dip continues.

runners_data.name: Carrigans Grove
runners_data.note: Gary Carroll partners a five-year-old who ran only 7 days ago and returns quickly — the headgear (p) is retained and while he has placed form over 7f on Good, a career-high 18th last time and no wins in his last eight starts make him difficult to back with conviction as a prominent runner in this competitive field.
runners_data.comment: Yet to win in five starts and often below-par, Carrigans Grove carries a notably higher speed rating (83) than her form suggests, and first-time cheekpieces plus a swift 7-day turnaround could spark improvement. Proven over today's trip and going but only tenth of fifteen, she has plenty to prove.

runners_data.name: Hugo's Girl
runners_data.note: W J Lee takes the ride on a mare with genuine recent form — 2nd and 3rd in her last four starts — but she is a true hold-up operator forced into a midfield position because this field is stacked with closers; her best efforts came at shorter trips (5-6f) and stepping to 7f on quick ground adds a query to an already compromised tactical picture.
runners_data.comment: Yet to win in five starts, Hugo's Girl has still been fairly consistent with three placed efforts including a second and two thirds. Quick to return within 7 days and already proven over today's distance, she's the type to go well without necessarily taking the top prize.

runners_data.name: Green Kite
runners_data.note: Colin Keane's booking is the headline angle, but this four-year-old has a fade-in-finish flag and only 3/7 similar-going runs in the money — a natural closer who is being mapped forward of her ideal position in this crowded rear-division, and that repositioning dulls the one asset (late kick) that makes her profile interesting.
runners_data.comment: Yet to win in five starts, Green Kite did show he retains ability with a solid second last time, though that followed moderate form including an eighth. Down in twelfth of fifteen on our figures with a modest speed rating (64), he's up against it here.

runners_data.name: Contrary To Law
runners_data.note: Ben Coen's tactical intelligence on an unknown-style three-year-old for J P Murtagh (2/22 in 14 days shows the yard is in decent nick) — only four runs to assess, all on Good or better with reasonable placing at 7f, but a blank win record and the uncertainty over natural running style make this a profile-watch rather than a confident selection.
runners_data.comment: Yet to win in four starts, Contrary To Law's form has been moderate, with a fourth three starts back the highlight. First-time hood may help following a 35-day break, and proven over today's distance, he sits mid-pack at sixth of fifteen on our figures.

runners_data.name: Unidos
runners_data.note: A three-year-old with a fade-in-finish flag and only 2/4 similar-going efforts in the frame — Ronan Whelan gets a chance, but an 8th, 12th and 16th in recent runs at various trips paint a picture of a horse yet to find his feet in handicap company, and the 26-day freshener has not transformed his profile significantly.
runners_data.comment: Yet to win in four starts and rarely competitive of late, with a fifth his best recent effort, Unidos sits low on our figures (61) and only thirteenth of fifteen. He's at least proven over today's distance, but there's little in the recent form to inspire confidence.

runners_data.name: Belle Nuit
runners_data.note: Chris Hayes partners a two-year-old returning after 248 days off the track — only three career runs to read from and the most recent was 15th at 8f on Heavy, though a 4th over 7f on Soft shows the trip is viable; the unknowable element of a long-absent juvenile is both the risk and the lure at a light weight of 129lbs.
runners_data.comment: Lightly raced with only three recent starts, Belle Nuit has yet to win but ran a fair fourth two starts back. She returns from a lengthy 248-day absence, and although proven over today's distance, the extended gap and thin sample make her hard to fully trust.

runners_data.name: Rappell
runners_data.note: Paul W Flynn's five-year-old carries a blinker (headgear: b) and goes again after just 7 days — a busy horse with a form string of 9-0-0-9-0-6 that offers little encouragement, and 0/13 in the trainer's last 14-day window reinforces the sense that connections are looking for a confidence run rather than expecting a major effort here.
runners_data.comment: Yet to win in six starts and rarely on the premises, Rappell carries a notably higher speed rating (76) than his placings suggest, and first-time blinkers could spark improvement. Proven over today's distance and going but only eleventh of fifteen, he remains hard to trust fully.

runners_data.name: Peig Sayers
runners_data.note: A fade-in-finish horse with a poor recent record (three 0s in last three runs) who is a natural hold-up type reassigned to midfield in this crowded field — Siobhan Rutledge rides, 57 days off the track, and a history of running over 8f rather than 7f makes the trip potentially too sharp for a horse who struggles to sustain even her modest efforts.
runners_data.comment: Yet to win in five starts, all of which have ended unplaced, Peig Sayers has a testing profile to turn around. Proven over today's distance with a slightly better speed figure (63) than her placings suggest, but fourteenth of fifteen on our figures, she's hard to fancy.

runners_data.name: Sonoma Sunset
runners_data.note: Neve Bennett (7lb) steers a four-year-old returning after 76 days — fade-in-finish flag is prominent in recent data and three runs at 7-10f on Standard or Good returned a 22nd, 9th and 10th; a natural closer who cannot get to her preferred rear position in this field shape, compounding an already difficult record on these conditions.
runners_data.comment: Yet to win in five starts and unplaced in three of her last four, Sonoma Sunset sits bottom of our figures at 46 and rock bottom on the speed figures too. Proven over today's distance, but everything about her recent form and figures points against her here.

races.paceDynamic: Faoladh is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 15-runner handicap and, crucially, faces no genuine pace rival to press him — meaning Andrew Slattery's four-year-old can slot comfortably to the front and dictate a controlled, sustainable tempo on what the going reports confirm is Good to Firm ground throughout the evening card. The prominent types Chester Nimitz, Loingseoir, Carrigans Grove and Rappell will push for early position and create a compact front group, but none is a natural pace-setter capable of running Faoladh off his feet, so the pace is likely to be honest rather than scorching. The field holds more hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear — Hugo's Girl, Green Kite, Peig Sayers and Sonoma Sunset are all genuine closers who will be forced to race closer to the pace than their natural style demands, reducing their ability to produce the late surge that suits them. A controlled early tempo on quick ground over 7f at Fairyhouse strongly favours horses racing prominently or just off the pace who can quicken from a good position in the straight — true hold-up horses are tactically compromised here.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Faoladh Controls, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Faoladh dictates an uncontested, even tempo and the prominent group track him into the straight, allowing a well-placed horse to pounce.
scenarios.body: Faoladh's lack of pace rivals lets him control every fraction, setting up a truly-run 7f where horses travelling prominently into the final two furlongs have first run on the hold-up brigade; on Good to Firm ground the strong gallop suits athletes who can sustain their effort rather than produce a single late burst.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Drifts Soft, Front Two Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Faoladh finds a slightly slower early tempo and the prominent group fail to pressurise, allowing the leader to coast and kick clear with a close tracker.
scenarios.body: A soft early pace on quick going can be a gift to a well-handled front-runner — Faoladh gets daylight, corners are negotiated smoothly, and the prominent horses camping on his quarters get first opportunity to mount a challenge that the hold-up horses simply cannot match from off the pace.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Closer Gets In
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves genuinely strong early and the prominent group fight for position, causing Faoladh to burn out and open the door for one fresher horse to motor through late.
scenarios.body: This scenario requires the prominent bunch to push fractions high enough that the front rank weakens inside the final furlong; Shoot To Kill is the hold-up horse with the most credible form at the trip to capitalise, though Hugo's Girl's strong recent form makes her the other candidate — both however are operating away from their ideal tactical scenario here.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Slips Through Rails
scenarios.trigger: If traffic patterns create a congested straight and a fresh-legged runner from a mid-race position threads through a gap on the rail that more fancied horses cannot reach.
scenarios.body: In a 15-runner handicap on quick ground the straight can become crowded as the hold-up horses attempt simultaneous runs, and a horse dropped quietly in midfield with a clean passage finds the gaps others cannot; Belle Nuit's 248-day absence is a concern but the unexposed profile at two is genuinely unknown, while Contrary To Law with Ben Coen's tactical intelligence could slot into an unlikely gap.

watchPoints.text: Faoladh unchallenged for lead — watch whether Adam Browne-Souza elects to stride on or is restrained, as any decision to slow the pace dramatically turns this into a sprint finish that could catch the prominent types flat-footed.

Chester Nimitz and Loingseoir both prominent types — if they push hard to track Faoladh in the early stages, the pace could quicken enough to burn out the front rank, creating a rare genuine closing opportunity for Shoot To Kill or Hugo's Girl.

Hugo's Girl and Green Kite are true hold-up horses mapped into midfield — watch whether W J Lee and Colin Keane attempt to drop them out to their natural position anyway, because if they do they will face an impossible task covering ground from the rear in a 15-runner handicap.

Belle Nuit represents a 248-day absence into a competitive handicap — Chris Hayes on the inside draw is the tactical angle to watch early; if she breaks cleanly and settles, the unknown fitness level becomes the only question.

Carrigans Grove runs just seven days after his last start — Gary Carroll's handling of a horse who has recorded 18th, 10th and 8th in recent outings suggests this could be a prep run, but watch for any early position gamble that might give connections information for a future target.
